doc.title: Mike Longo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2019

title: Advice for a young player: polymetric time
summary: Practice, study and learn polymetric time with African drumming touch; Mongo's sacred rhythms.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Wow. If you had a niece or nephew that was headed towards a career in jazz, would you have any real-life advice that you might tell them?

Yeah. Practice. Study and practice. Digest. And also, I would teach them the polymetric time. Because most of the people in the colleges are playing with the wrong time conception, man. They’re playing the notes they hear Charlie Parker play, but they’re playing with a time conception that comes from European music, which is monorhythmic. It’s not polymetric time. And so a big part of it is learning the right time conception. And the piano starts playing — Charlie Parker said he felt like the saxophone was playing itself. So often times that happens to me on the piano, man. The piano is doing stuff — where did that come from, you know. So I’m just going where the music is telling me, man, but you have to be playing with the right touch so that you’re playing with a touch that is activated by African drumming. I remember Mongo used to make mention of sacred rhythms.
